issues: No sign of gaming the measurement. The diff adds no file or network access, pastes no answers and does not touch test labels. It only changes the fingerprint radius (2 to 3), switches from bit fingerprints to count fingerprints, and changes the Tanimoto denominator to use squared norms.

No bug that would make the result meaningless. For count vectors, A·B/(|A|²+|B|²−A·B) is the standard continuous Tanimoto similarity. For binary vectors it gives the same result as before, because A² = A. The 1e-9 floor still prevents division by zero.

Recomputed z ≈ 0.27, which matches the harness value of 0.271. The difference is 0.4830 − 0.4803 = 0.0027. The noise sd for the difference of two single runs is 0.0070·√2 ≈ 0.0099, so z = 0.0027/0.0099 ≈ 0.27.

The candidate is better by 0.0027, well within the noise, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers. Each side has only one run. A replicate would be needed to tell whether this small gain is real.
